title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
Problem (§18): turn the alternating series s = 1/α − 1/β + 1/γ − 1/δ + … into a continued fraction. The preceding pages (§§13–17) reached this result by a roundabout route through a general continued fraction. Here Euler gives the 'direct method' he promised in §17.

Method: take the tails t = 1/β − 1/γ + 1/δ − … and u = 1/γ − 1/δ + …. Then s = 1/α − t = (1 − αt)/α, so 1/s = α/(1 − αt) = α + α²t/(1 − αt) = α + α²/(−α + 1/t). The same identity applied to each tail gives 1/t = β + β²/(−β + 1/u), 1/u = γ + γ²/(−γ + 1/v), and so on. Substituting these in turn gives Theorem I:
1/s = α + α²/(β − α + β²/(γ − β + γ²/(δ − γ + …))).

In modern terms each step is the one-step tail recursion r_k = 1/a_k − r_{k+1}. Inverting it gives the continued fraction whose convergents equal the partial sums of the series. This is Euler's continued-fraction form of a series.

Examples (§19):
- α_k = k gives 1/ln 2 = 1 + 1²/(1 + 2²/(1 + 3²/(1 + …))).
- α_k = 2k − 1 gives 4/π = 1 + 1²/(2 + 3²/(2 + 5²/(2 + …))). Euler identifies this as Brouncker's continued fraction.

§20: s = ∫₀¹ x^{m−1}dx/(1 + x^n) = 1/m − 1/(m+n) + 1/(m+2n) − …. This gives 1/s = m + m²/(n + (m+n)²/(n + (m+2n)²/(n + …))). The formula is completed on the next page, where Euler says he had already given it in Comm. Acad. Petrop. Tom. XI.
errors: None in the mathematics. All the identities check: α/(1−αt) = α + α²t/(1−αt) = α + α²/(1/t − α), and the substitutions give the stated partial denominators β−α, γ−β, …. The examples for ln 2 and π/4 are correct. Convergence is not discussed, but it is automatic here because the convergents equal the partial sums of the series.

ideas.what: Direct derivation, via the tails of the series, of the continued fraction equivalent to an alternating series of reciprocals
ideas.modern_name: Euler's continued fraction formula (series-to-continued-fraction equivalence, convergents = partial sums)
ideas.where_published: Introductio in analysin infinitorum I (E101, 1748), ch. 18; E123 'De fractionibus continuis observationes' (Comm. Petrop. 11); E593 itself

ideas.what: Continued fraction for 1/ln 2 with partial numerators k² and partial denominators 1
ideas.where_published: E123 and related continued-fraction papers (exact location unsure)

ideas.what: Recovery of Brouncker's continued fraction for 4/π from the Leibniz series
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brouncker (published by Wallis, 1656); derivation from the Leibniz series by Euler

ideas.what: Continued fraction for ∫₀¹ x^{m−1}/(1+x^n) dx with partial numerators (m+kn)² and partial denominators n
ideas.modern_name: Continued fraction for a Beta-type (digamma-difference) integral
ideas.where_published: E123 (Comm. Acad. Petrop. 11), as Euler himself states

deep.surprise_reason: This is Euler's well-known series-to-continued-fraction transformation, already in the Introductio (1748). The examples (log 2, Brouncker, the Beta-type integral) are standard, and Euler explicitly cites his own earlier paper. The tail-recursion derivation is elementary and widely reproduced.
